name: Password Store
author: Jonny Heggheim
description: pass, the standard unix password manager, as an Omarchy launcher: press a key, type to search your store by site or username, then copy or type a password, username or OTP code. Add and edit entries in a masked form with a reveal, a colour-coded readout and a generator. Copies carry the password-manager hint so the clipboard history never records them, and the clipboard is cleared after a minute. gpg-agent can ask for passphrases with an Omarchy-styled prompt. First open walks a new seat through the GPG key, pass init and how the vault syncs (local, git, rclone or a custom command).

barWidget.description: Bar button for the Password Store search overlay; holds its settings

schema.label: Vaults
schema.description: JSON array of vault records, one per password store: {id, name, storeDir, gpgIds, syncBackend, gitRemote, gitPullOnOpen, rcloneRemote, rcloneMode, rclonePullOnOpen, syncPushCmd, syncPullCmd}. The setup card (F2) maintains it; by hand, omarchy bar set … vaults '[…]' without --json (the array arrives as a string and is parsed back). Empty: the single store described by the keys below.

schema.label: Active vault
schema.description: The id of the vault the card searches. Tab in the card switches it.

schema.label: Password store directory
schema.description: One-store installs without a vaults array: the store. Leave empty to use $PASSWORD_STORE_DIR or ~/.password-store, exactly as pass does. Vaults carry their own storeDir.

schema.label: Clear the clipboard after (seconds)
schema.description: Copied passwords, usernames and OTP codes are cleared from the clipboard after this long, and scrubbed from the clipboard history should it have recorded one (copies carry the password-manager hint, so it normally does not). Also passed to pass as PASSWORD_STORE_CLIP_TIME for the terminal actions.

schema.label: Username field names
schema.description: Comma-separated keys, matched case-insensitively against the 'key: value' lines of an entry. Falls back to the second line of the entry.

schema.label: Store entries as name/username
schema.description: On: an entry's last path segment is its username (github.com/jack), so the list shows both without decrypting and the editor names new entries that way. Off: pass's classic folder/entry layout; the row shows the folder under the entry and the username stays inside the file.

schema.label: Allow typing into the focused window (Ctrl+Enter)
schema.description: Ctrl+Enter types the password, Ctrl+Shift+Enter the username, using wtype. Off, only the clipboard actions remain.

schema.label: Show a notification when something is copied
Sync backend
schema.description: One-store installs: local (nothing leaves this machine), git (pass git push after a change), rclone (rclone copy/sync to a configured remote) or custom (your own push/pull commands). Vaults carry their own. The setup card (F2) fills this in.

schema.label: git remote URL
schema.description: https or ssh URL of the store's origin. Credentials stay with git and ssh.

schema.label: git: pull --rebase when the card opens
rclone remote path
schema.description: remote:path of an rclone remote you have already configured with `rclone config`. Tokens stay in rclone's own config.

schema.label: rclone push mode
schema.description: copy never deletes anything on the remote; sync makes the remote match the store, deletions included.

schema.label: rclone: copy from the remote when the card opens
custom: push command
schema.description: Run with bash -lc in the store after a change; $STORE is the store directory. Never put a secret in it.

schema.label: custom: pull command
schema.description: Run with bash -lc in the store when the card opens. May be empty.

schema.label: Wrong passphrases before a lockout
schema.description: Counted by pinentry-omarchy across requests within ten minutes; the card and the helper refuse to decrypt while locked.

schema.label: First lockout (seconds)
schema.description: Each further lockout is four times longer, up to thirty minutes. A decrypt that works resets everything.

schema.label: Lock the session at the longest lockout
schema.description: Off by default. On, reaching the thirty-minute tier also runs omarchy-system-lock, on the theory that the seat is not in its owner's hands.
